question.text: The electric field associated with a light wave is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>.57</mo><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>7</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>ct</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mfenced></math> (where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></math> are in metre and second respectively). This light is used in an experiment on photoelectric effect with the emitter having work function <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">ϕ</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext>1.9</mtext><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mn>e</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. What is the maximum kinetic energy (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>eV</mi></math>) of the ejected photoelectron? [Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>14</mn></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>hc</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12400</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi><mo> </mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>∘</mo></mover></math>]

solution.text:
Given, E=E0sin⁡1.57×107x-ct ...(i)
∴E=E0sin⁡ωcx-ct ...(ii)

On comparing equations (i) and (ii), we get
ωc=1.57×107
     =π2×107
λ=4×10-7 m
  =400 nm

As, ϕ0=hcλ-EK
1.9=1240400-EK
EK=3.1-1.9 eV=1.2 eV
